parts.name: Left ventricle
parts.info: The strongest chamber. It pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve to the whole body.
parts.fact: Its wall is about 1 cm thick, roughly three times thicker than the right ventricle's.

parts.name: Right ventricle
parts.info: Pumps oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary valve to the lungs.
parts.fact: It forms most of the front surface of the heart.

parts.name: Interventricular septum
parts.info: The muscular wall between the two ventricles. It also carries the electrical wiring that times each beat.
parts.fact: A hole in this wall (ventricular septal defect) is one of the most common heart defects at birth.

parts.name: Left atrium
parts.info: Receives oxygen-rich blood from the four pulmonary veins and passes it to the left ventricle.
parts.fact: Atrial fibrillation, the most common heart rhythm problem, usually starts near where the pulmonary veins enter.

parts.name: Right atrium
parts.info: Receives oxygen-poor blood from the body through the superior and inferior venae cavae.
parts.fact: The heart's natural pacemaker, the sinoatrial node, sits in its wall.

parts.name: Mitral valve
parts.info: Two leaflets between the left atrium and left ventricle. They stop blood flowing backward when the ventricle squeezes.
parts.fact: Named after a bishop's mitre, because its two cusps look like the hat.

parts.name: Tricuspid valve
parts.info: Three leaflets between the right atrium and right ventricle.
parts.fact: The closing of the mitral and tricuspid valves makes the first 'lub' of the heartbeat.

parts.name: Aortic valve
parts.info: Three half-moon cusps at the exit of the left ventricle into the aorta.
parts.fact: The coronary arteries branch off just above this valve.

parts.name: Pulmonary valve
parts.info: Three cusps at the exit of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
parts.fact: The closing of the aortic and pulmonary valves makes the second 'dub' sound.

parts.name: Papillary muscles
parts.info: Finger-like muscles inside the ventricles. Through thin cords they hold the valve leaflets shut against pressure.
parts.fact: If a papillary muscle tears after a heart attack, the mitral valve can suddenly leak.

parts.name: Right coronary artery
parts.info: Supplies the right side of the heart and usually the back of the septum, including the heart's pacemaker cells.
parts.fact: In roughly 70–85% of people it gives rise to the posterior descending artery.

parts.name: Left coronary artery
parts.info: Splits into the left anterior descending and circumflex branches that feed most of the left ventricle.
parts.fact: A blockage of the left anterior descending artery is nicknamed the 'widow-maker'.

parts.name: Cardiac veins
parts.info: Drain used blood from the heart muscle into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.
parts.fact: The great cardiac vein runs alongside the left anterior descending artery.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.info: The body's main artery. It rises from the left ventricle, arches over the heart and runs down to the abdomen.
parts.fact: At its root it is about 3 cm wide.

parts.name: Pulmonary trunk & arteries
parts.info: Carry oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs. The only arteries that carry oxygen-poor blood.
parts.fact: The trunk splits into right and left pulmonary arteries just under the aortic arch.

parts.name: Pulmonary veins
parts.info: Four veins that bring oxygen-rich blood from the lungs into the left atrium.
parts.fact: They are the only veins that carry oxygen-rich blood.

parts.name: Superior vena cava
parts.info: Returns blood from the head, neck and arms to the right atrium.
parts.fact: It has no valves, so blood pressure in it is close to the pressure in the right atrium.

parts.name: Inferior vena cava
parts.info: Returns blood from the legs and abdomen to the right atrium. It is the widest vein in the body.
parts.fact: It passes through the diaphragm at about the level of the eighth thoracic vertebra.
